comments.body:
Are you able to reproduce this by following the instructions yourself using a normal `ubuntu:22.04` image?

I've seen similar errors when installing some ROS-related packages before adding the ROS apt repo, which was installing ROS packages from the Ubuntu system packages instead of the ROS apt repo. Example: https://packages.ubuntu.com/jammy/python3-rosdep2

comments.body:
I've dug into it a little bit today, and the issue seems to be that `ros-dev-tools` depends on `python3-bloom`, which depends on `python3-rosdep2`, at least on humble.
As a workaround, I have uninstalled `ros-dev-tools` and installed its dependencies manually, except for `python3-bloom`, and that seems to work, run `sudo apt install ros-build-essential python3-colcon-common-extensions python3-colcon-mixin python3-rosdep python3-vcstool wget` (or your preferred package manager) and that might fix it for now.

comments.body: Interesting! `python3-bloom` from the ROS apt repo (search for `Package: python3-bloom` in http://packages.ros.org/ros2/ubuntu/dists/noble/main/binary-amd64/Packages) does apparently depend on `python3-rosdep2`, but I think we want `python3-rosdep` (provided by the ROS apt repo) and _not_ `python3-rosdep2` (provided by the Ubuntu system packages).
comments.bodyHTML: Interesting! python3-bloom from the ROS apt repo (search for Package: python3-bloom in http://packages.ros.org/ros2/ubuntu/dists/noble/main/binary-amd64/Packages) does apparently depend on python3-rosdep2, but I think we want python3-rosdep (provided by the ROS apt repo) and not python3-rosdep2 (provided by the Ubuntu system packages).

comments.body: I used the Wayback machine to look at an older version of http://packages.ros.org/ros2/ubuntu/dists/noble/main/binary-amd64/Packages, see https://web.archive.org/web/20250426211604/http://packages.ros.org/ros2/ubuntu/dists/noble/main/binary-amd64/Packages. If you find `Package: python3-bloom`, which was version 0.12.0 vs version 0.13.0 now, you see that it does _not_ depend on `python3-rosdep2`. Only `python3-rosdep`. So something went wrong there.

If you find Package: python3-bloom, which was version 0.12.0 vs version 0.13.0 now, you see that it does not depend on python3-rosdep2. Only python3-rosdep. So something went wrong there.

comments.body: This is a known issue - when the package is built on newer Ubuntu versions, debhelper automatically resolves the Python dependencies to deb packages and incorrectly chooses the system's provider for `rosdep2` instead of the one packaged by the ROS team. We'll need to re-build and re-release the package.

comments.body: Should the release be reverted until a new release can be built? Would unblock quite a few CIs / users.
